concern_results.conclusion: The Ruby scanner now reads its input as raw bytes. It replaces invalid UTF-8 only in the copy used for the regex search, and still hashes the original bytes for the waiver check. The parts joined into each output record are all byte strings, so the join should not raise an encoding error. The repo-hygiene checker now counts only the script a command actually runs, plus the test files given to pytest, unittest, node --test and run-parallel-suites.sh. The test selector now runs the hygiene check for every test filename shape it enforces and for MANIFEST.json files under eval/evidence/.

The extra Git options in host-smoke.sh are -c core.fsmonitor=false and -c safe.directory=<repo>. Git accepts safe.directory from the command line, and the trust is limited to that one repository path. The change only reads the repository; it adds no write path and changes no permissions.

A line with invalid UTF-8 no longer aborts the scanner, and a real Ruby failure still blocks the gate through the md_ref_scan_rc check. One small gap: if the repo path contains a symlink that differs from the path Git resolves, safe.directory may not match. That is not blocking.

The new tests would fail if the old behaviour came back. These are: (b4) the invalid-byte line must still report the missing citation with no scan error; the hygiene check must reject files that only appear as script arguments; the selector must trigger on each shape; and the stub git refuses to run without safe.directory. The ruby stub that simulates a failure was updated to the new source text, so it still triggers.
Every change answers an open item from the previous review and stays inside the Batch A scope. Command-line flags and gate output tokens are unchanged, and no extra flags or layers were added.
These are tooling and doc changes only, with no migration step; each one can be reverted on its own.
The md_reference_scan_error marker, the unregistered-test-file messages and the host-smoke git failure output are all still in place.
The claims of 25/25 mutations and 0.70s / <0.10s timings cannot be checked from the diff, but the code is consistent with them. docs/npm-release.md now describes the four-host smoke.
The shared-gate change closes a gap: test files that only appear as script arguments are no longer counted as registered. The release-smoke Git trust change is limited to the repository path.

The host-smoke changes follow the scripts/AGENTS.md rules on tracked-file staging and env scrubbing. The source-register change only adds a row, and the validator changes come with self-tests. I found no rule broken.
